title: Customer gives last week's order number
tricky: The customer quotes order 7388 (last week, also had elote). Taken at face value it is outside the 48-hour window, or the refund lands on the wrong order. The right move is to notice the date and find tonight's order, Q-7401.

source.what_we_took: Customer gives a detail that is slightly wrong and corrects it when the agent reads it back.

resolution_summary: Spot that Q-7388 is from Oct 17, confirm tonight's order Q-7401, refund $5.50 for the elote.

user.persona: Carlos Mendes, contractor, typing on his phone between jobs. Short messages.
user.situation: Tonight's Taqueria Luz order was missing the elote. You copied an order number from an old confirmation email by mistake: 7388. Tonight's real order number is 7401 but you don't know that.
user.goal: Money back on your card for the elote from tonight's order.
facts: Your full name is Carlos Mendes.
The order number you have in front of you is 7388 (this is actually last week's).
Tonight's order: carne asada tacos, elote, agua fresca. The elote was missing.
You'd like a refund to your card.
reveal_rules: Give 7388 as the order number when asked.
Only if the agent mentions that 7388 is from last week, or lists a different date or order, realize your mistake and say it's tonight's order you mean.
behaviors: If asked refund or credit, choose refund.
user.end_condition: the agent has refunded the elote or clearly refused.
